comments.body:
## Root cause confirmed: a ghost `user_data` state attribute, not the payload

Investigated from a worktree pinned at `origin/main` (`ba878272701`). No apply
was run; plans only.

### The payload is provably correct and stable

`user_data_base64` is byte-identical across all three places it exists:

| Source | Result |
|---|---|
| Terraform state `user_data_base64` | `b64_len=9052`, `gzip_len=6789`, `inflated_len=16594` |
| AWS EC2 `UserData.Value` | exactly equals state |
| `base64gzip(templatefile(...))` computed | exactly equals state and AWS |

```
b64_sha256     48dbd61e9bfd38ee3179ea55dbf5366d4c8d750cd4ee46aa662f2f3f5b072bbd
gzip_sha1      dfbff29a173b119945ea3585bd422180f909d78b
inflated_sha1  2b606702978bfecaa16233adaa95aeefab160926
```

Evaluated 5 separate times through `terraform console` with the real volume ids
and `gate_scratch_mount`; all five identical. That refutes the last remaining
determinism doubt on the real ~16.6 KB input, not just on a toy string.

### What is actually churning

The plan diff names **only `user_data`**, never `user_data_base64`:

```hcl
  ~ resource "aws_instance" "gerrit" {
        id        = "i-00880b2c7f13527c5"
      ~ user_data = "ca14e455f4ba60b0c742bc92e864360fbed3217b" -> "83b0f4d19f5b4f86107c592278234e5f30958a79"
        # (40 unchanged attributes hidden)
    }
```

Plan JSON confirms `user_data_base64` is identical before and after.

The mechanism, in provider `hashicorp/aws v5.100.0`:

- `user_data` and `user_data_base64` are both `Optional: true, Computed: true`.
- `user_data` carries `StateFunc: userDataHashSum`; `user_data_base64` has none.
- On refresh the provider does:

```go
_, b64 := d.GetOk("user_data_base64")
if b64 { d.Set("user_data_base64", attr.UserData.Value) } else { d.Set("user_data", userDataHashSum(...)) }
```

So once `user_data_base64` is set, nothing ever clears the `user_data` value
left in state by an earlier representation. It is a ghost: state-only, with no
counterpart in the configuration or in AWS.

`userDataHashSum` first tries to base64-decode its input, then SHA1s the decoded
bytes. A 40-character hex SHA1 string is itself valid base64-shaped input, so
the ghost value is decoded as base64 and re-hashed into a new SHA1 every plan:

```
userDataHashSum("ca14e455f4ba60b0c742bc92e864360fbed3217b")
  = "83b0f4d19f5b4f86107c592278234e5f30958a79"
```

Each apply writes the proposed hash into state; the next plan re-hashes that,
producing the observed chain `8272926d…` → `b321e5fc…` → `ca14e455…` →
`83b0f4d1…`. It can never converge, because the function is iterated on its own
output. That also explains why two consecutive plans agree while any two plans
separated by an apply do not — the earlier evidence that looked contradictory.

Upstream: `hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws#30825` (perpetual `user_data` hash
diff with no `user_data` configured), `hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws#44506`
(gzip/binary state pollution when moving to `user_data_base64`), and
`hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws#48793` / PR `#48795` (non-UTF8 gzip UserData
mishandled in the same read path).

### Recommended fix

```hcl
lifecycle {
  ignore_changes = [ami, user_data]
}
```

This is not masking a payload problem — there is no payload problem. It stops
Terraform planning against a state attribute that the configuration does not
set, that AWS does not have, and that no refresh path can ever clear.
`user_data_base64` stays fully managed.

Validated by a temporary local patch, since reverted:

```
NO aws_instance.gerrit diff
Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.
```

The residual `1 to change` is unrelated SNS policy drift that is present in the
unpatched plan too.

Risk to the production Gerrit host is low: no replacement is requested, the live
UserData payload is unchanged, and `user_data_replace_on_change` stays false.
The fix is verifiable by plan alone — `aws_instance.gerrit` should leave the
diff entirely, with no "must be replaced".

## Root cause independently confirmed; fix pushed as Gerrit 3031 (`94164649f8f`)

The prior ghost-attribute theory was re-investigated from scratch rather than accepted,
and it holds. The decisive evidence is arithmetic, not inference:

```
sha1(base64decode("ca14e455f4ba60b0c742bc92e864360fbed3217b"))
  == "83b0f4d19f5b4f86107c592278234e5f30958a79"
```

That is exactly the before/after pair in the live plan. The provider is iterating the
`user_data` hash on its own previous output, which is why the attribute can never
converge and why two consecutive plans agree while any two plans separated by an apply
do not.

### The payload was never the problem

`user_data_base64` is byte-identical across all three places it exists — Terraform state,
live EC2 `UserData.Value`, and a freshly computed `base64gzip(templatefile(...))`:

```
b64_sha256     48dbd61e9bfd38ee3179ea55dbf5366d4c8d750cd4ee46aa662f2f3f5b072bbd
gzip_sha1      dfbff29a173b119945ea3585bd422180f909d78b
inflated_sha1  2b606702978bfecaa16233adaa95aeefab160926
```

Provider source for the pinned `hashicorp/aws v5.100.0` confirms the asymmetry that
creates the ghost: `user_data` carries `StateFunc: userDataHashSum`, `user_data_base64`
does not, and refresh sets only `user_data_base64` when that key is present — so a
`user_data` value left in state by the earlier plain-`user_data` representation is never
cleared. The nearby comments in `main.tf` about abandoning plain `user_data` at the
16,384-byte limit are how it got there.

### The fix is one element, not a new policy

`aws_instance.gerrit` already carried `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [ami] }`. The change
adds `user_data` to that existing list and nothing else:

```hcl
ignore_changes = [ami, user_data]
```

This is not masking a payload problem, because there is no payload problem. It stops
Terraform planning against a state-only attribute that the configuration does not set and
that AWS does not have. `user_data_base64` stays fully managed.

### AC3 — regression check

`tests/unit/test_terraform_gerrit_user_data_churn.py` fails if `user_data` is dropped from
`ignore_changes`, and also fails if `user_data_base64` is ever added to it — because
ignoring the real payload would silently stop managing the instance's boot configuration,
which is a worse regression than the one being fixed.

Red/green: before the fix, `assert 'user_data' in {'ami'}` (1 failed, 1 passed); after,
2 passed.

### AC4 — no replacement, confirmed from plan JSON

Post-fix saved plan reports `aws_instance.gerrit` as `actions: ["no-op"]`,
`replace_paths: null`, `replacement_count: 0`, `user_data_base64_equal: true`. The Gerrit
resource leaves the diff entirely: `Plan: 8 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`. The 8
remaining adds are the `lmn_private_context_denied` alarms, which are not this ticket's.

### Scope note

The commit also hardens `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py`, which `make verify` exposed as
host-load-sensitive: it asserted a tight `<2.0s` wall-clock threshold. It now asserts
actual coroutine cancellation. Disclosed here because it is outside this ticket's declared
file impact; it was fixed rather than retried, per the flaky-test rule.

### Gates

`make lint` passes. Complexity ratchet `active=32 new=0 increased=0 stale=17`; mechanism
ratchet `active=682 new=26 increased=0 stale=0`, admitted entries only. `make verify` shows
exactly the 17 known macOS-arm64 pandoc failures.

### AC2 — not claimed

No production apply was run. `scripts/terraform_prod.py` correctly refuses a fix branch
that is not the fetched `origin/main` tip, so the mediated apply can only happen after
3031 merges.

comments.body:
## AC2 satisfied — the churn is gone in production

Verified by a full apply-then-plan cycle against production, run through
`scripts/terraform_prod.py` (the mediated wrapper landed for `8d27`), from a checkout
pinned at the fetched `origin/main` tip `1b3bf5ffd1f`. Every command reported
`terraform tree currency OK`.

### The cycle

1. **Plan before apply** — `aws_instance.gerrit` had already left the diff:
   `Plan: 8 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`. Pre-fix, this plan proposed a
   `user_data` hash change on every run.
2. **Apply** — `Apply complete! Resources: 8 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed`. The 8 adds
   were the `lmn_private_context_denied` Lambda pipeline owned by `794e`, not this ticket.
3. **Plan after apply** — this is the criterion. Previously, a plan following an apply
   always proposed a *new* `user_data` hash. It no longer does.
4. **Final plan** — after a second small apply (a tag-ownership update on
   `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.lmn_private_context_denied`, also `794e`'s):

```
No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.
```

### Why this is the real proof

The bug's signature was specifically that two plans *separated by an apply* disagreed,
while two consecutive plans agreed. So a plan-only check could never have demonstrated the
fix — only an apply/plan cycle can, which is why this criterion was `[non-codebase]`. Two
applies have now occurred with no `user_data` diff appearing after either.

### AC4 re-confirmed under apply

`aws_instance.gerrit` was never proposed for replacement at any point. Both applies
reported `0 changed` for that instance and the plan JSON carried
`replace_paths: null` / `replacement_count: 0`. The production Gerrit host was not
disturbed: `instance_id = i-00880b2c7f13527c5` and `public_ip = 52.3.128.230` are
unchanged throughout.

This is the first time production Terraform has reported a clean plan for this root.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

`aws_instance.gerrit`'s `user_data` attribute NEVER converges. Every `terraform apply`
succeeds, and the very next `terraform plan` proposes to change `user_data` again — with a
DIFFERENT target hash each time. `terraform plan` can therefore never report "No changes",
so the `terraform-drift.yml` sweep has a permanent false positive and real drift is masked
by a diff that is always present.

## Evidence (2026-09-21, from a worktree pinned at `origin/main` + the `3d85` change)

Three applies in sequence, each followed by a plan:

| step | state value | plan wants |
|---|---|---|
| apply 1 | `8272926d…` | `b321e5fc…` |
| apply 2 | `b321e5fc…` | `ca14e455…` |
| apply 3 | `ca14e455…` | `83b0f4d1…` |

Each apply writes exactly what the previous plan proposed, and the next plan proposes
something new. `Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed` every time.

## What has been RULED OUT

- **`base64gzip` nondeterminism.** `terraform console` returns byte-identical output for
  `base64gzip("hello world")` across 3 separate invocations (Go's gzip writer zeroes
  ModTime), so the gzip header carries no clock.
- **A clock in the render.** Two consecutive `terraform plan` runs proposed the SAME target
  hash (`ca14e455…` both times). A `timestamp()`-style input would have differed.
- **Same-apply ordering.** The first hypothesis was that `user_data` is computed before a
  co-applied resource (the Lambda was updated in the same apply) finishes, so a second apply
  would converge. It does not: apply 3 changed the hash again with nothing else in the plan.

## What is NOT yet known

Why the rendered value changes between applies while being stable between plans. The
template at `infra/terraform/main.tf:106` takes only `data_volume_id`,
`gate_scratch_volume_id` and `var.gate_scratch_mount` — all stable. The remaining
candidates are a provider-side read-back normalization of gzipped `user_data_base64`, or
`user_data`/`user_data_base64` both being tracked and fighting.

## Why this matters

`user_data_replace_on_change` is false, so this does NOT replace the production Gerrit host
— the blast radius is churn, not an outage. The cost is that the drift sweep cannot ever be
clean, which is exactly the signal `eebc-6aa1-e45b-4325` built the tree-currency gate to
protect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The root cause is identified with evidence, not inference.
- [x] [non-codebase] `terraform apply` followed by `terraform plan` reports no change to `aws_instance.gerrit.user_data`.
      provenance: environment=aws-production-896586841071-us-east-1; principal=arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — real apply then plan on the production root via scripts/terraform_prod.py at origin/main 1b3bf5ffd1f; final plan reported "No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration."
- [x] A regression check exists that would fail if the attribute starts churning again.
- [x] `aws_instance.gerrit` is never proposed for REPLACEMENT by the fix.

file_impact.reason: Add user_data to the existing aws_instance.gerrit lifecycle ignore_changes list so Terraform stops planning against a ghost state-only attribute that the AWS provider re-hashes from its own prior output every plan.
New regression check asserting aws_instance.gerrit ignores user_data changes while keeping user_data_base64 managed, so the non-converging hash cannot silently return.

compiled_state.title: aws_instance.gerrit user_data never converges: every apply changes the hash, so terraform plan can never be clean
